vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes skip the Sunday schedule and get their own label so they stand out.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Weekly refresh of transitive dependencies, which no other rule updates (Scorecard found fixed CVEs sitting in the lockfile). Runs in the same Sunday-evening window as everything else.

packageRules.description: House-style titles: config:recommended sets chore/fix per package, so override it here; later rules set CI and FFmpeg.
SHA-pinned actions in one PR; Renovate rewrites the SHA and the version comment.
npm minor and patch updates in one PR; majors one by one.
Our own SDK is published from this repo's CI with provenance: no release-age wait (as in pnpm's minimumReleaseAgeExclude).
Node.js: the base image, .node-version, engines and @types/node move together on the LTS line CI and the image run; majors by hand.
The Docker base image, pinned by digest next to its tag.

ffmpeg in the image: Renovate can't write a release note, so its PR gets the no-change label like every update (without it the release-note check fails until someone adds one by hand). The PR text asks the reviewer to swap the label for a note when users would notice the update.
prBodyNotes: **Release note:** this updates the ffmpeg that Transcoda runs. If users would notice it (new hardware support, a fixed encode or decode bug, a changed default), remove the `no user-facing change` label and add a `.changes/` note before merging; see `.changes/README.md`.

customManagers.description: Jellyfin's ffmpeg build, installed from their apt repository in docker/Dockerfile.
